questions.stem: About the gonadal activity of the ovary:
options: Its endocrine function is the secretion of estrogens and progesterone
Its exocrine function corresponds to oogenesis
In women, reproductive activity is continuous between puberty and menopause
In men, gonadal activity declines with age but does not completely cease
questions.explanation: The ovary has an endocrine (hormones) and an exocrine (gametes) function. Female reproductive activity is CYCLICAL and limited to puberty–menopause; male activity is continuous and only declines with age.

questions.stem: About the ovary:
options: The ovarian cortex contains the various stages of folliculogenesis
The medulla is loose connective tissue rich in blood and lymphatic vessels and nerves
Each ovary measures about 3 cm in width and 1 cm in length
Folliculogenesis takes place in the medulla
questions.explanation: Folliculogenesis happens in the cortex (periphery); the medulla is the vascular central part. Each ovary is about 1 cm wide and 3 cm long, not the reverse.

questions.stem: About the female genital tract:
options: The Fallopian tubes measure 10 to 14 cm and partially cover the ovaries
From outside to inside, the uterine wall comprises the serosa, the myometrium and the endometrium
Cervical mucus selects and facilitates the passage of spermatozoa into the uterine cavity
The myometrium is the layer whose thickness and secretory activity vary during the cycle
questions.explanation: The myometrium is a thick smooth-muscle layer; it is the endometrium (mucosa) whose thickness, vascularization and secretion vary with the cycle.

questions.stem: About the primordial follicle:
options: Primordial follicles start to form around the 7th month of gestation
It contains a primary oocyte arrested in prophase I, surrounded by a few flattened follicular cells
At birth each ovary contains about one million primordial follicles
Between birth and puberty folliculogenesis is active and the follicular reserve increases
questions.explanation: Between birth and puberty folliculogenesis is quiescent and about 60% of the reserve degenerates; the stock is non-renewable.

questions.stem: An ovary contains about 1,000,000 primordial follicles at birth, and about 60% of them degenerate before puberty. About how many remain in this ovary at puberty?
questions.explanation: 40% of 1,000,000 = 400,000 per ovary, the figure the lesson gives for puberty. 600,000 is the number that degenerated, not the number left.
questions.mental: What remains is 100 − 60 = 40%: 0.4 × 10⁶ = 4 × 10⁵ = 400,000. 600,000 is the trap (the degenerated part); 4,000,000 is more than you started with, so it is impossible.

questions.stem: Which features distinguish a primary follicle from a primordial follicle?
options: A single layer of cuboidal (instead of flattened) follicular cells
The appearance of a zona pellucida between the oocyte and the follicular cells
An oocyte arrested in prophase I
An undifferentiated theca separated from the follicular cells by the Slavjanski membrane
questions.explanation: Both follicles contain a primary oocyte arrested in prophase I, so this does not distinguish them. The primary follicle adds cuboidal cells, a zona pellucida, a theca and the Slavjanski membrane.

questions.stem: About the secondary and tertiary (cavitary) follicles:
options: In the secondary follicle, the follicular cell layers multiply to form the granulosa
The theca interna is fibrous and the theca externa is cellular
In the tertiary follicle, fluid-filled antral cavities appear within the granulosa
In the tertiary follicle, the theca interna cells acquire the ability to secrete estrogens
questions.explanation: The theca splits into an inner CELLULAR theca interna (which becomes estrogen-secreting) and an outer FIBROUS theca externa.

questions.stem: About the mature (Graafian) follicle:
options: It reaches about 2.5 mm in diameter
Its antral cavities fuse into a single antrum folliculi filled with follicular fluid
The innermost layer of the cumulus oophorus, adjacent to the zona pellucida, becomes the corona radiata
The first polar body is expelled outside the zona pellucida
questions.explanation: The Graafian follicle is about 2.5 cm wide. When meiosis I is completed a few hours before ovulation, the first polar body stays WITHIN the zona pellucida.

questions.stem: Concerning the histological section (figure), which statement(s) is (are) correct?
options: It is a mature (Graafian) follicle
Cavity 5 is filled with follicular fluid and results from the fusion of the antral cavities
Layer 3 derives from the innermost layer of the cumulus oophorus, next to structure 2
Layer 4 is the theca interna
questions.explanation: 1 = oocyte, 2 = zona pellucida, 3 = corona radiata, 4 = granulosa, 5 = antrum folliculi. A single large antrum marks the mature follicle; layer 4 is the granulosa (follicular cells), not a theca.

questions.stem: About ovulation:
options: It occurs under the influence of an LH and FSH surge and of the pressure of the follicular fluid
The cell expelled from the ovary is the primary oocyte
The oocyte leaves with the zona pellucida, the corona radiata and part of the cumulus oophorus, and enters the outer third of the Fallopian tube
It occurs about 36 hours after the LH peak
questions.explanation: The primary oocyte completes meiosis I a few hours before ovulation, so the expelled cell is the SECONDARY oocyte arrested in metaphase II.

questions.stem: The yellowish colour of the corpus luteum is due to:
options: Lutein pigment secreted by the luteinized follicular cells
Estrogens secreted by the theca interna
The thecal capillaries that invade the granulosa
The remains of the degenerating oocyte
questions.explanation: After the Slavjanski membrane disappears, thecal capillaries grow into the granulosa and the follicular cells become luteinized cells secreting lutein pigment, which gives the yellow colour (luteinization).

questions.stem: About the fate of the corpus luteum:
options: In the absence of fertilization it becomes a gestational corpus luteum
In case of fertilization it persists for about three months, then the placenta takes over steroid production
Its degeneration gives the corpus albicans, which is phagocytosed by macrophages
The menstrual (progestational) corpus luteum lives about three months
questions.explanation: Without fertilization it is a menstrual (progestational) corpus luteum living about 14 days; only with fertilization does it become gestational and persist about three months.

questions.stem: In the corpus luteum, which cell–hormone pairs are correct?
options: Lutein cells derived from the granulosa → progesterone
Theca interna → estrogens
Granulosa lutein cells → estrogens only
Theca externa → progesterone
questions.explanation: Granulosa cells become lutein cells that secrete progesterone, while the theca interna keeps producing estrogens.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old competitive runner with low body weight consults for irregular cycles. Based on the lesson:
options: Intense physical activity may delay ovulation
Low body weight can disturb ovulation
Such ovulatory disorders are generally reversible
Obesity, by contrast, has no effect on ovulation
questions.explanation: Both excess weight (obesity) and low weight or eating disorders disturb ovulation; vigorous exercise can delay it, and these dysfunctions are generally reversible.

questions.stem: About the uterine cycle (average 28 days):
options: The endometrium reaches its maximal thickness during the secretory phase
The proliferative phase is marked by the 'uterine lace' pattern
The average 28-day duration is identical in all women
The first day of menstruation marks the beginning of a new cycle
questions.explanation: The 'uterine lace' (spiral arteries, tortuous glands) belongs to the secretory phase; the proliferative phase is regeneration with gland elongation. 28 days is only a conventional reference.

questions.stem: In the absence of fertilization, menstruation is triggered by:
options: Regression of the corpus luteum 10–12 days later, with a sharp fall in progesterone and estrogens
The LH surge
A rise in estrogen secretion
The formation of a new corpus luteum
questions.explanation: The progestational corpus luteum regresses, progesterone and estrogen levels fall, and the endometrium detaches.

questions.stem: Concerning the diagram of the uterine lining (figure), which statement(s) is (are) correct?
options: In phase I, the endometrium is shed, leaving a thin residual layer
Phase II corresponds to days 14–28
In phase III, glands become tortuous and glycogen secretion increases
The corpus luteum shown above phase III contains lutein cells secreting progesterone
questions.explanation: I = menstrual phase (days 0–4), II = proliferative phase (days 4–14), III = secretory phase (days 14–28), which follows ovulation and the formation of the corpus luteum.

questions.stem: About the multiplication phase of oogenesis:
options: It involves the oogonia, diploid stem cells dividing by mitosis
It occurs during embryonic and fetal life
Oogonia are located in the medullary zone of the embryonic ovary
Most oogonia degenerate around the 7th month of intrauterine life
questions.explanation: Oogonia lie in the CORTICAL zone of the embryonic ovary; they multiply only before birth, giving a non-renewable stock of primary oocytes.

questions.stem: Which chromosome number / DNA content pairs are correct?
options: Primary oocyte after DNA replication: 2n, 4q
Secondary oocyte: n, 2q
First polar body: n, q
Oogonium: n, 2q
questions.explanation: Meiosis I splits the primary oocyte (2n, 4q) into a secondary oocyte and a first polar body that are both n, 2q. Oogonia are diploid (2n).

questions.stem: About the growth phase of oogenesis:
options: The primary oocyte greatly increases in size
It involves intense synthesis of RNA and proteins needed for fertilization and early development
Primary oocytes do not complete meiosis I before puberty because of a meiosis-inhibiting factor secreted by follicular cells
Fewer than 500 oocytes will reach ovulation during a woman's reproductive life
questions.explanation: All four are stated in the lesson: of about 400,000 follicles left at puberty, fewer than 500 ovulate.

questions.stem: About the maturation phase of oogenesis:
options: The first meiotic division is highly unequal, the secondary oocyte keeping most of the cytoplasm
The second meiotic division arrests in prophase II
Without fertilization, the oocyte completes meiosis and then degenerates
If fertilization occurs, meiosis is completed, giving the ovum (ovotide) and a second polar body
questions.explanation: Meiosis II arrests at METAPHASE II and is only completed if a spermatozoon fertilizes the oocyte; otherwise the oocyte is expelled, still in metaphase II, and degenerates.

questions.stem: A primary oocyte completes oogenesis after fertilization. How many ova (functional female gametes) does it give?
questions.explanation: Female meiosis is unequal: one primary oocyte gives a single ovum, the other products being polar bodies. Compare spermatogenesis, where one spermatocyte I gives 4 spermatids.

questions.stem: Concerning the diagram of oogenesis (figure), which statement(s) is (are) correct?
options: Cell 1 multiplies by mitosis during embryonic and fetal life
Cell 2 is arrested in prophase I and is already present at birth
Cell 3 is arrested in metaphase I
Cell 5 forms even in the absence of fertilization
questions.explanation: 1 = oogonium, 2 = primary oocyte, 3 = secondary oocyte (arrested in METAPHASE II), 4 = first polar body, 5 = ovum, which forms only if a spermatozoon penetrates.

questions.stem: About the hypothalamic–pituitary control of the ovary:
options: FSH rises during the follicular (preovulatory) phase and peaks together with LH at ovulation
The main LH surge occurs about 36 hours before ovulation and induces progesterone secretion
Progesterone inhibits FSH secretion, while estrogens inhibit LH release
GnRH is released at a rate of two to three pulses per day
questions.explanation: Feedback is the other way round: progesterone inhibits LH and estrogens inhibit FSH. GnRH pulses occur two to three times per HOUR.

questions.stem: Which hormone promotes follicular growth and estradiol production?
options: FSH
LH
Progesterone
GnRH
questions.explanation: FSH promotes follicular growth and estradiol production; LH triggers ovulation and progesterone secretion, and GnRH acts on the pituitary.

questions.stem: In a 25-year-old woman, the oocytes held in the primordial follicles of her ovaries:
options: Are primary oocytes arrested in prophase I
Were formed before her birth
Are continuously renewed by mitoses of oogonia
Are haploid
questions.explanation: The stock of primary oocytes (2n) is formed in fetal life and is non-renewable; oogonia no longer divide after birth.
